I keep hearing the same birthright-citizenship defense from institutional conservatives I respect: “150 years of settled meaning.”

It’s wrong twice.

First, the modern universal rule was never settled in the way they’re claiming.

The original statutory formula was “born in the United States” and “not subject to any foreign power.” Congress kept that formulation in federal law until 1940, when it recodified citizenship using the 14A’s wording.
